findings.label: M-01
findings.title: Underwater-pool migration is bricked by requested-vs-received accounting mismatch
findings.description: StableStaker.migrateOut (src/StableStaker.sol:301-337) returns amounts[i]=requested (line 324) to the migrator but only transfers payout=_routeExit(...,false) (line 334), which can be less than requested when the strategy is below par. StableStakerMigrator.migrate (src/StableStakerMigrator.sol:46-65) then forceApprove(Sum(requested)) (line 57) and depositFor(requested) in a loop (line 60) using the reported requested amounts, not the actually-received payout. When underwater, received < requested, so the approve/depositFor accounting exceeds the tokens on hand.
findings.impact: The migration escape hatch atomically reverts whenever the strategy is below par. No fund loss and no state corruption, but the intended escape-hatch availability is denied precisely when users most need to exit an underwater pool.

findings.label: M-02
findings.title: Underwater withdraw buffer is FCFS at par, socializing strategy loss onto slow stakers
findings.description: StableStaker._routeExit (src/StableStaker.sol:494-502) returns par from the buffer branch (line 498), reached from withdraw (line 258). While the strategy is underwater, withdraw pays full par out of a finite shared buffer on a first-come-first-served basis.
findings.impact: Late/slow stakers are forced into the emergency or migrate paths and absorb the full shortfall, while early withdrawers are made whole from the shared buffer. Loss is socialized FCFS rather than pro-rata. External precondition: the strategy is underwater.

findings.label: C-01
findings.title: rescueERC20 can sweep the buffer backing underwater withdrawals
findings.description: StableStaker.rescueERC20 (src/StableStaker.sol:521-528) computes reserved=0 when a strategy is set (line 523), so the owner can sweep the entire buffer that backs underwater withdrawals.
findings.impact: Owner-only operation over protocol-owned funds; no theft of accounted principal. Centralization risk: a trusted owner could remove the buffer that backstops withdrawals while underwater. QA bundle.

findings.label: L-01
findings.title: Unbounded per-user external-call loop in migrateOut/migrate
findings.description: StableStaker.migrateOut calls phUSD.mint inside a per-user loop (src/StableStaker.sol:327) and StableStakerMigrator.migrate calls depositFor inside a per-user loop (src/StableStakerMigrator.sol:60). Both loops are unbounded by user count.
findings.impact: Large user sets can exceed the block gas limit. Permissioned and recoverable via paging. QA bundle.

findings.label: L-02
findings.title: Unused return value of EnumerableSet.add/remove
findings.description: StableStaker ignores the boolean return value of EnumerableSet.add (lines 233, 361) and EnumerableSet.remove (lines 250, 287, 323).
findings.impact: Benign; the success boolean is not checked but the operations are idempotent in context. QA/Info bundle.
